ai.title: OpenTUI native bundle install gets recovery and staging logic
ai.summary: The CLI build now sources its OpenTUI native bundle from a staging directory written to by ensureOpenTuiNativeBundle, which seals the bundle with a .freebuff-native-bundle.json receipt of sha256 file hashes and swaps it atomically so a stale split install fails before the binary step. prepareOpenTuiNativeBundle resolves both @opentui/core and @opentui/react up front, runs bun install with --os and --cpu flags into the staging root, and replaces the old patchOpenTuiAssetPaths and tar-based fetch path in build-binary.ts.
ai.evidence: cli/scripts/open-tui-native-bundle.ts is a new file that defines the functions ensureOpenTuiNativeBundle, getValidBundleVersion, sealOpenTuiNativeBundle and the type OpenTuiNativeTarget, which cli/scripts/build-binary.ts calls via prepareOpenTuiNativeBundle after resolving both @opentui/core and @opentui/react versions up front in getInstalledOpenTuiPackage.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer or release flow relies on the new receipt file or how the recovery directory cleanup is scheduled across builds.

facts: Keep the parsed query synchronized with the text that selection handlers mutate. A deferred query can lag by one keystroke, causing Enter or Tab to replace the wrong range in the current input.
The cursor position must match the text being parsed. Using a deferred input with the current cursor causes desync during heavy renders.

ai.title: Add user-only skills and fix suggestion input sync
ai.summary: Skills can now be marked user-only via the disable-model-invocation frontmatter flag, which is parsed into disableModelInvocation and read by isSkillModelInvocable so the agent runtime keeps user-only skills out of model discovery and surfaces a 'can only be invoked by the user' error instead. The skill handler also honors the highest-precedence on-disk skill and no longer advertises user-only cached skills in suggestions. The CLI suggestion engine now parses inputValue directly instead of a deferred value, keeping the cursor and typed text in sync during heavy renders. Skill commands in the slash menu gain insertText so selecting a skill inserts /skill:<name> into the input.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies common/src/types/skill.ts to add the 'disable-model-invocation' boolean field to the SkillFrontmatterSchema and a matching disableModelInvocation field to SkillDefinitionSchema, introduces createSkillDefinition to map frontmatter into a SkillDefinition, and adds isSkillModelInvocable + filter calls in common/src/util/skills.ts, packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/skill.ts, and sdk/src/skills/load-skills.ts. The agent runtime skill handler adds the isUnavailableToModel check and returns a 'can only be invoked by the user' error when disableModelInvocation is true. The suggestion engine removes useDeferredValue in use-suggestion-engine.ts so slashContext and mentionContext parse inputValue directly, and the slash command builder adds insertText to skill commands in cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts.
ai.migration: If you author skills, add disable-model-invocation: true to a skill's SKILL.md frontmatter to restrict it to explicit user invocation.
ai.unknowns: The rollout status of user-only skills to the agent registry and whether the provisioned tier surfaces them differently.

entries.title: CLI update: smoke-terminal-broker-windows

ai.title: Windows terminal health reporting and watchdog arming telemetry
ai.summary: The CLI introduces a new windows-terminal-health module that centralizes Windows terminal-failure reporting for both the command broker and the terminal watchdog, routing events through PostHog when analytics is initialized and otherwise queuing them directly into the Axiom shipper before draining. cli/src/index.tsx now drains queued client logs right after the APP_LAUNCHED event on Freebuff Windows launches, so a health row ships before the PowerShell watchdog is armed and survives an endpoint-security kill of that spawn for rapid-resume on the next --continue launch. The watchdog is no longer opt-in via CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG on Windows; it is armed by default and suppressed only by the existing CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG escape hatch, with a 10-second WINDOWS_ARM_TIMEOUT_MS arming monitor reporting a timeout if the armed marker is never written. A new TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED event joins TERMINAL_BROKER_SPAWN_FAILED in the always-track analytics set, and the broker's old sanitizeTerminalBrokerVersion helper is replaced by sanitizeWindowsCliVersion in the shared health module.
ai.evidence: The diff adds cli/src/utils/windows-terminal-health.ts, which defines `reportWindowsTerminalFailure`, `deliverWindowsTerminalFailure`, `sanitizeWindowsCliVersion`, and the `WindowsTerminalHealthDeliveryDeps`/`WindowsTerminalFailure` types, and is imported by cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts and cli/src/utils/terminal-watchdog.ts (both replacing their old inline reporting). cli/src/index.tsx now calls `drainClientLogs()` for IS_FREEBUFF on win32 after APP_LAUNCHED. cli/src/types/env.ts and cli/src/utils/env.ts drop `CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG`. common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts adds `TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED = 'cli.terminal_watchdog_failed'`, and common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts adds it to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS`.
ai.migration: No action is required; Freebuff Windows users now get the watchdog armed by default instead of needing CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG, and those who rely on the opt-in variable to avoid it should keep setting CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that reads the new always-track TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED events in dashboards, or the rollout state of arming the watchdog by default for all Freebuff Windows users.

ai.title: suggestfollowups prompts shift to goal-oriented phrasing
ai.summary: The suggest_followups tool now enforces short, goal-oriented prompt generation across base-chat, base2, and base-deep agents. This change updates the tool description, parameter schema, and type definitions to explicitly exclude implementation steps, file paths, and manual user chores from suggested followups. The modification affects agents/types/tools.ts, common/src/tools/params/tool/suggest-followups.ts, and related agent templates. Followup prompts must now name the desired outcome in one sentence, allowing the agent to determine the execution strategy.

eli5.text: When you click a suggested followup prompt, it now sends a short, outcome-focused question instead of a long, step-by-step instruction. The assistant's suggestions are shaped by clearer guidance that favors naming the goal over listing files or chores. Because the rule is shared across chat and deep research agents, you get consistent, goal-oriented prompts wherever you click a suggestion.

ai.title: Add bookmark gate analytics events
ai.summary: Added `FREEBUFF_BOOKMARK_GATE_SHOWN` and `FREEBUFF_BOOKMARK_GATE_CONFIRMED` to `AnalyticsEvent` enum. Tracks blocking bookmark prompt after first prompt in Web/Cloud workspaces. Enables measuring abandon rate via event delta. Scope: `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`.

eli5.text: When you open the app for the first time in a browser, you'll now see a small pop-up asking you to save a bookmark before you can continue working. The app records whether you see that pop-up and whether you click the bookmark button, so the team can count how many people close the tab instead of continuing. That count is the key number they're watching, since the pop-up doesn't have any other way to skip it. The change is live today for anyone opening the app in a web or cloud workspace.

facts: a suggested followup should be phrased, shared by every agent that ends its turn with suggest_followups.

ai.title: Unify followup style guidance across agents
ai.summary: Extracted duplicated prompt instructions into a shared `FOLLOWUP_STYLE_GUIDANCE` constant in `agents/constants.ts`. `base-deep.ts` and `base2.ts` now import this constant instead of embedding inconsistent inline text. The `suggest-followups.ts` tool description was updated to clarify that suggestions must be actionable by the agent, removing the 'manual work' prohibition in favor of tool-aware judgment.

eli5.text: If you've ever asked an AI agent to suggest follow-up steps at the end of a conversation, you may have noticed the examples were slightly different depending on which agent gave them, one might say 'Split this file up' while another said 'Add unit tests.' Now, every agent pulls those suggested follow-ups from the same guidance, so the phrasing is consistent no matter which agent you're talking to. Behind the scenes, the duplicated instructions were moved into one shared reference that all the agents read from, and the note telling the agents how to phrase those suggestions was updated to focus on outcomes rather than specific files or steps. If you looked, you'd see each agent still suggests roughly three next steps, but the wording and style match across all of them.

eli5.text: The developers split a single testing deadline into two separate timers: one for letting the program boot up (now 15 seconds) and another for how long it should stay alive after its companion program is killed (now 6 seconds). This fixes a problem where a slow startup on a crowded testing machine would eat into the time the program was allowed to keep running, making real bugs invisible under a generic timeout. Only the testing setup changed, no feature you can touch was affected, and nothing new is live today for you to use.
